target_customer: Life science and biotech companies making regulated products (GxP labs and GMP manufacturers)
problem: Regulated manufacturers run batch records, quality, MES, ELN and LIMS in separate systems and paperwork. Seal puts them in one workspace with an AI agent that drafts documentation for review.
product_category: Regulated life sciences workspace (QMS, MES, ELN, LIMS)

founders.name: Will Moss
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder of Opvia (Seal's earlier name; legal entity Opvia Ltd). Aggregator profiles say Cambridge chemical engineering, data scientist, Entrepreneur First; not confirmed in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Regulated-grade document and data workflows across lab and manufacturing systems need validation and integration work; the later AI agent adds more.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance records and validated workflows are hard to migrate once adopted, but early Opvia was a small lab tool in a field with established ELN vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found. CB Insights auto-generated pages pair it with Benchling, Labstep and Labguru, which is not dated evidence.

market_need_then: Biotech labs adopt electronic lab notebooks and quality systems for compliance. No dated 2019 to 2020 demand evidence was found in opened sources.

branding.domain_note: Uses seal.run, not an exact .com; the legal entity remains Opvia Ltd.

rebrands.why: Not found; date unknown. Inferred from the legal entity name Opvia Ltd on the site and Seal listed as the product.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name with many unrelated companies named Seal in search results, and no brand press found.

pivots.from: Opvia, pitched as an AI bioprocess company
pivots.to: Seal, all-in-one workspace for regulated products

outcome_analysis: Seal, formerly Opvia, is an active London company with a stated 40 person team, offices in the UK and US, and 50 plus customers per its own site. Public funding evidence is weak: one job-board listing shows a small 2020 seed and nothing later was found. Its growth story and defensibility cannot be judged from public sources.
notes: Welcome to the Jungle listing (seen via search summary) shows one 0.2M seed in 2020-09, single aggregator, so not recorded as a round. No Series A or press release found. joinef.com page returned 404. Competitors: CB Insights comparison pages are undated and auto-generated; none recorded. Rebrand from Opvia to Seal: relation is inferred from the YC page naming Opvia and the Opvia Ltd legal entity, date unknown.
